attacks.claim: TRAILING_PUNCT is an unanchored `+$` regex. On a long run of punctuation inside a URL-like match it backtracks quadratically. Descriptions are owner-controlled, have no length cap, and are tokenized on every item page load for every neighbor, so one crafted description can freeze the UI thread.
attacks.evidence: const TRAILING_PUNCT = /[.,;:!?)\]]+$/; ... const raw = m[0].replace(TRAILING_PUNCT, ''); ABSENT: any maximum length for item.description or for a URL token

attacks.claim: TRAILING_PUNCT always strips a closing ')', so balanced-parenthesis URLs such as Wikipedia-style paths are cut short and point to the wrong page. The stripped ')' is left as visible text, which hides the error.
attacks.evidence: const TRAILING_PUNCT = /[.,;:!?)\]]+$/; (e.g. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drill_(tool) links to ...Drill_(tool and renders ')' as plain text)

attacks.claim: The stated invariant that truncation only cuts at whitespace or between tokens is contradicted by the hard-cut branch for a leading text token with no whitespace. The test suite codifies that behaviour, so the PR overstates the guarantee. A URL that fails new URL() is kept as text and can also be split by this branch.
attacks.evidence: "truncation only cuts at whitespace or between tokens" vs. "else if (out.length === 0) out.push({ kind: 'text', value: Array.from(t.value).slice(0, limit).join('') });"

attacks.claim: A leading link is shown whole with no length bound and no overflow/word-break rule, so a very long URL at the start can fill the phone screen and defeat the collapse. A link after the limit is dropped entirely, which makes leading and mid-text links behave inconsistently.
attacks.evidence: "a leading link is shown whole rather than collapsing to nothing" / out.push(t); ABSENT: any CSS change for overflow-wrap or word-break

attacks.claim: When the cut falls in a text token, only text before the last whitespace is kept. A long unbroken non-URL run after an early word can shrink the collapsed view to a fragment, hiding the owner's content behind 'Show more' for no benefit.
attacks.evidence: const cut = head.search(/\s\S*$/); if (cut > 0) out.push({ kind: 'text', value: head.slice(0, cut) });

attacks.claim: Length accounting mixes UTF-16 units (value.length, slice) with code points (Array.from), so the 280 budget is applied inconsistently for non-BMP text such as emoji. The collapsed output can exceed 280 UTF-16 units.

Expansion state is local useState and is not keyed to the item. If the component instance is reused for a different item, the new description can open expanded. If text shrinks below the limit while expanded is true, the stale state carries over to the next long text.

Owner-supplied external http(s) links become clickable for every signed-in neighbor. Previously the text was inert. The PR adds no warning, allowlist, reporting path, or moderation step, and does not mention the phishing risk. rel attributes are set and javascript: URLs are excluded, so the risk is product-level rather than an injection bug.
attacks.evidence: {t.value}; ABSENT: any mention of unsafe-link handling or reporting

attacks.claim: Links open in a new window with no indication to screen-reader users. The toggle label also changes between 'Show more' and 'Show less' while aria-expanded already conveys state, so the announcement is redundant.
The change renders on every item page but has no feature flag or kill switch. A rendering regression can only be fixed by revert or redeploy.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: feature flag or gating for ItemDescription; the diff only touches ItemPage.tsx and new web/src/items files

attacks.claim: Tests miss paths the PR relies on: the 'Show less' transition back to collapsed, the exact 280-character boundary (not truncated), a balanced-parenthesis URL, and an unparseable http(s) candidate near the cut point.
attacks.evidence: ItemDescription.test.tsx has two component tests and three truncate assertions; no test asserts 'Show less' or text.length === 280
